correctness.rationale: For a unit disk, illumination is exactly strict containment in the lattice triangle and the distance is one plus the largest center-to-vertex radius. Assuming radius at most \(\sqrt5\), strict side distances give area greater than half the perimeter; triangle isoperimetry and lattice half-integrality force area \(11/2\) or \(6\), while the circumdisk bound excludes larger half-integral values. Squared lattice side lengths are sums of two squares at most 20. Fresh exact Heron enumeration gives only (8,20,20), (9,17,20), (10,13,17), (10,16,18) and (13,13,16), every one containing a side of length at least four. Its strict side-line distance then forces an endpoint beyond radius \(\sqrt5\), contradiction. The explicit family has all three side distances greater than one and converges to the bound.
